newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil bolsa to buy trade system to boost capacity.
newsitem.headline: Brazil bolsa to buy trade system to boost capacity.

text.p: The Sao Paulo stock market, Brazil's largest bolsa, has agreed to buy a $20 million trading system from the Paris bourse that would boost its trading capacity sixfold, an official said.
Alfredo Rizkallah, president of Sao Paulo's Bovespa exchange, said the system, called NSC, would allow it to increase capacity to 120,000 transactions a day from 20,000 transactions currently.
Rizkallah said the Sao Paulo bolsa decided to buy the technology to increase competitiveness and accommodate an expected rise in volume next year.

The Bovespa expects average daily turnover to reach $700 million by the end of 1997, compared with a current $380 million, mainly because the growth of private pension plans has boosted domestic savings, he said.
He also said the NSC system would allow brokerages to develop new trading strategies.

"This trading program will permit the development of new trading products," he said, adding it will make viable some small transactions such as trading in shares of smaller companies that are privatized.
Currently, the Sao Paulo bourse has two trading systems -- a live-voice system and an electronic system known as the CATS. The NSC system will replace both.
Installation is expected to begin in June 1997. The project will cost an initial $5 million, with the price tag rising to $20 million by the time the system is completed, officials said.
